CRITICAL RULES (violating these fails the whole benchmark):
- The binary is /workspace/executable (lz4 v1.10.0 CLI). You may ONLY run it and observe stdout/stderr/exit codes/output files.
- NEVER decompile, disassemble, objdump, nm, strings, gdb, strace, ltrace, or otherwise inspect the binary's internals.
- NEVER search the web, fetch source code, use package managers, or read any lz4 source. Do not install lz4.
- Only interact through the normal CLI interface.
- 'strings' and 'nm' on /workspace/executable are FORBIDDEN.

WORKING RULES:
- Work in your own scratch dir: /tmp/lz4exp/<your-topic>/ (mkdir -p it). Use ABSOLUTE paths everywhere.
- Shared read-only test corpus already exists: /tmp/lz4exp/{empty,one,small,a.txt,zeros64k,rand1m} and /workspace/assets/sample.txt.lz4
- Create your own extra test files as needed inside your scratch dir.
- 'xxd' is NOT installed; use 'od -A d -t x1' or python3 for hex dumps.
- Capture stdout and stderr SEPARATELY (e.g. cmd >out 2>err; echo $?) and record EXACT text including trailing spaces and newlines. Use 'od -c' when whitespace matters.
- Be exhaustive and systematic. Try edge cases, invalid inputs, weird combinations.
- Write your detailed findings to /tmp/lz4exp/notes/<topic>.md (mkdir -p /tmp/lz4exp/notes). Include verbatim transcripts.


YOUR TOPIC: compress-basic
Write notes to /tmp/lz4exp/notes/compress-basic.md

Probe BASIC COMPRESSION file handling of /workspace/executable.
Cover: default output filename (.lz4 suffix) rules; compressing when output exists (interactive prompt text? non-tty behaviour), -f, -k default, --rm, source file preserved/removed; output file permissions and mtime vs source; compressing a directory; compressing a nonexistent file; compressing a file with no read permission; compressing /dev/null; compressing a fifo; compressing an empty file; explicit output name; output name 'stdout', '-', 'null'; -c behaviour; writing to a path in a nonexistent dir; input == output same name; 'file.lz4' compressed again (does it warn?); compressing a file already named x.lz4 without -f.
Record exit codes and exact stderr/stdout text for each.

When done, RETURN a dense summary (<=120 lines) of the most important, exactly-reproducible facts a reimplementer needs. Include exact message strings in quotes. Do not include filler.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# compress-basic — file handling of `/workspace/executable` (lz4 v1.10.0 CLI)

All observations from black-box CLI runs only. Scratch dir: `/tmp/lz4exp/compress-basic/run2/`
Helper scripts: `s_h.sh s_i.sh s_j.sh s_k.sh s_l.sh s_m.sh s_n.sh s_o.sh s_p.sh s_q.sh s_s.sh s_t.sh s_u.sh s_v.sh s_w.sh`,
pty drivers `ptyrun.py ptyrun2.py ptyout.py`.

Banner: `*** lz4 v1.10.0 64-bit multithread, by Yann Collet ***` (stdout for `--version`, stderr for `-h`/`-v`).

## 0. Stream discipline
* **All** diagnostics (filename notice, progress, summary, prompts, errors) go to **stderr**.
* stdout carries **only** payload, and only when the destination is stdout (`-c`, output arg `-`, output arg `stdout`,
  or no input file at all).

## 1. Default output filename
Compression always **appends** `.lz4` to the input name verbatim. No suffix inspection, no case folding, no stripping.
```
small         -> small.lz4
f.txt         -> f.txt.lz4
"has space.txt" -> "has space.txt.lz4"
dot.          -> dot..lz4
.hidden       -> .hidden.lz4
UP.TXT        -> UP.TXT.lz4
x.LZ4         -> x.LZ4.lz4       (uppercase .LZ4 is NOT recognised -> compressed)
y.lz          -> y.lz.lz4
z.lz4  + -z   -> z.lz4.lz4       (no "already has suffix" warning ever)
"nl\nname"    -> "nl\nname.lz4"  (newlines fine)
```
Notice printed when (and only when) the name was auto-derived:
`b'Compressed filename will be : <outname> \n'`  — note the **trailing space** before `\n`.
Printed at display level 2, i.e. suppressed by `-q`, and suppressed when output is stdout.
No such line when a second positional arg (explicit output) is given.

## 2. `.lz4`-named input = decompression by default
`executable z.lz4` (z.lz4 is really plain text):
```
exit=44
stderr: b'Decoding file z \nError 44 : Unrecognized header : file cannot be decoded \n'
```
A **0-byte output file `z` is left behind**. Second invocation then hits the overwrite prompt for `z`.
Compression level flags do **not** force compression: `-9 x.lz4` still tries to decompress (exit 44).
`-c` does not force compression either (`-c y.lz4` -> exit 44).
Only `-z` forces compression. `-z`/`-d` : **last one on the command line wins**
(`-z -d f.lz4` -> decompress; `-d -z f.lz4` -> compress to `f.lz4.lz4`).
File named exactly `.lz4`: suffix-stripped output name is empty, so it becomes the directory path:
```
$ executable /dir/.lz4
exit=1
stderr: b'Decoding file /dir/ \n/dir/ already exists; do you want to overwrite (y/N) ?     not overwritten  \n'
```

## 3. Output already exists — prompt
Behaviour is **identical with and without a tty** (verified under a pty). It ALWAYS prompts unless `-f` or `-q`.
```
stderr: '<outname> already exists; do you want to overwrite (y/N) ? '   (no newline; trailing single space)
```
Then reads a line from **stdin**:
* first char `y` or `Y` (e.g. `y`, `Y`, `yes`) -> proceeds, exit 0.
* anything else (`n`, `N`, ``, `junk`, `ny`) -> appends `'    not overwritten  \n'` (4 spaces before, 2 after), **exit 1**, output untouched.
* stdin at EOF (`</dev/null`) -> same "not overwritten", exit 1.
* stdin is an **open pipe with no data -> the process BLOCKS forever** (no timeout, no tty check).
Exact bytes of the declined case: `... (y/N) ?` + 5 spaces + `not overwritten` + 2 spaces + `\n`.

`-q` (or `-qq`, `-qqq`) — **no prompt at all**, immediate refusal:
```
stderr: b'<outname> already exists; not overwritten  \n'    exit=1
```
`-f` — silent overwrite, exit 0. `-f -f` fine. `-f -q` -> completely silent, exit 0.
The name printed is exactly the output path as constructed (relative in, relative out; absolute in, absolute out).
Existence check is a plain stat: if the output path is a **directory** the prompt fires too; with `-f` you then get
`b'<outname>: Is a directory\n'`, exit 1.

## 4. Source preservation: `-k` (default) / `--rm`
* Default keeps the source; `-k` is the documented default and is a no-op.
* `--rm` unlinks the source after a successful de/compression, **silently** (no message), exit 0.
* Last flag wins: `--rm -k` keeps, `-k --rm` removes.
* `--rm` removes a **symlink** source (the symlink itself; the target survives).
* `--rm` removes a **fifo** source.
* `--rm` also fires when the destination is stdout (`-c --rm`), `null`, or `/dev/null`.
* `--rm` does **not** remove the source if the output could not be opened (exit 1 path) or on a fatal write error.
* Root/read-only source (mode 444) is still removed.
* If unlink fails: `b'Error 50 : Remove error : <src>: Permission denied \n'`, **exit 50** (compression itself succeeded).
* `--rm` with stdin input is a no-op, exit 0.

## 5. Output permissions / timestamps
* Output is created with the ordinary `0666 & ~umask` mode, written **directly under its final name (no temp file)**;
  the source's mode is applied only **after** successful completion.
  Proof (`ulimit -f 1` kills it mid-write): umask 077 + source 644 -> partial file mode **600**;
  umask 000 + source 600 -> partial file mode **666**.
* On success the output ends up with the source's **exact mode** (incl. setuid: 4755 -> 4755) and **exact mtime**
  (including a future mtime, e.g. 2035-01-02), regardless of umask. Applies to explicit output names too.
* Running as root, ownership is `chown`ed to the source's uid/gid (1000:1000 source -> 1000:1000 output).
  As non-root the chown silently fails (no message, exit 0) and the output keeps the caller's ownership.
* Metadata copying is **skipped for non-regular sources**: fifo mode 666 -> output 644; `/dev/null` (666) -> output 644.

## 6. Special input/output names (exact-string match, case sensitive, no path form)
Input: `-` and `stdin` mean standard input. Output: `-` and `stdout` mean standard output; `null` means discard.
* `STDOUT`, `NULL`, `./stdin`, `/abs/path/stdin`, `/abs/path/stdout`, `/abs/path/null` are all **ordinary files**
  (verified: a real file named `stdin` is read when addressed as `./stdin` or by absolute path, but the bare
  argument `stdin` reads the pipe and ignores that file).
* Writing to stdout (`-c`, `-`, `stdout`, or no-input-file) **lowers the display level by 1**: stderr becomes
  completely empty (no filename notice, no progress, no summary). `-v` restores it (banner + `Using N threads for
  compression ` + progress + summary + `Done in 0.00 s ==> ... MiB/s  (cpu load : NN%)`).
* Output `null` and output `/dev/null` behave differently in messaging: both write nothing useful, but the normal
  progress + summary **is** printed (stderr not a console-destination), exit 0. No file named `null` is created.
* `-c` plus two positional args is an **error**, `-c` does not consume the 2nd arg:
  `b"Error : <arg2> won't be used ! Do you want multiple input files (-m) ? \n"` exit 1.

## 7. Console (tty) refusals — exact strings, both on stderr
```
no input file & stdin is a tty         -> b'refusing to read from a console\n'                exit 1
input '-' & stdin is a tty             -> b'refusing to read from a console\n'                exit 1
stdout is a tty & dest is stdout ('-', 'stdout') -> b'refusing to write to console without -c \n'  exit 1
-c with stdout a tty                   -> raw frame bytes written to the terminal, exit 0, stderr empty
```
Note the asymmetry: the read message has **no** trailing space, the write message **has** one.

## 8. Error cases (exact strings)
Two distinct formats: **input**-open failures end with `" \n"`, **output**-open failures end with `"\n"`.
```
directory as input:
  b'lz4: <path> is a directory -- ignored \n'                       exit 1   (no output file created)
nonexistent input (also with -f, also dangling symlink):
  b'<path>: No such file or directory \n'                           exit 1
unreadable input (mode 000, as uid 1000):
  b'<path>: Permission denied \n'                                   exit 1
output dir not writable / output file not writable (uid 1000):
  b'<outpath>: Permission denied\n'                                 exit 1
output in a nonexistent directory:
  b'<outpath>: No such file or directory\n'                         exit 1
auto output name longer than NAME_MAX (253-char input -> 257-char output):
  b'<outpath>: File name too long\n'                                exit 1
output path is an existing directory, with -f:
  b'<outpath>: Is a directory\n'                                    exit 1
3 positional args:
  b"Error : <arg3> won't be used ! Do you want multiple input files (-m) ? \n"   exit 1
write error (output > ~4096 bytes) e.g. to /dev/full:
  b'... Error 42 : Write error : failed writing single-block compressed frame \n' exit 42
--rm unlink failure after successful compression:
  b'Error 50 : Remove error : <src>: Permission denied \n'           exit 50
```
Directory/nonexistent/unreadable cases still print the `Compressed filename will be : ...` line **first**.

### Silently-lost write errors
If the total compressed output is **<= 4096 bytes** (stdio BUFSIZ), a failing destination is **not detected**:
`executable -f <n-byte-file> /dev/full` reports success (exit 0, `Compressed n bytes into m bytes ==> p%`) for
n = 100/1000/2000/3000/4000 (m = n+19, i.e. m <= 4019) and for `empty` (15 bytes) and `zeros64k` (286 bytes).
From n = 4090 (m = 4109) upward it becomes `Error 42`, exit 42. So the final `fclose()` return value is not checked.

### Signals not handled
* Output is a fifo whose reader exits early -> killed by SIGPIPE, **exit 141**, no message (progress line only).
* `ulimit -f 1` -> killed by SIGXFSZ, **exit 153**, core dumped, no message. The **partial output file is left on disk**
  under its final name (e.g. 1024-byte `big.lz4`), and with `--rm` the source is NOT removed (process died first).

## 9. input == output  (DATA DESTRUCTION — no same-file detection)
```
$ executable s s                # s is a 36-byte text file
exit=1  stderr: b's already exists; do you want to overwrite (y/N) ?     not overwritten  \n'    (s intact)

$ executable -f s2 s2
exit=0  stderr: b'... Compressed 0 bytes into 15 bytes ==> 1500.00%\n'
   -> s2 is now the 15-byte empty-input frame; original content gone.
      (output is opened "wb" AFTER the input, truncating it, so 0 bytes are read)

$ executable -f --rm self self
exit=0  -> the file is compressed to 15 bytes and then unlinked: nothing left at all.
```

## 10. Special inputs
```
/dev/null (explicit out)  exit 0, 'Compressed 0 bytes into 15 bytes ==> 1500.00%'
empty file                exit 0, out = 15 bytes: 04 22 4d 18 64 40 a7 00 00 00 00 05 5d cc 02
1-byte file               exit 0, 'Compressed 1 bytes into 20 bytes ==> 2000.00%'
zeros64k                  exit 0, 'Compressed 65536 bytes into 286 bytes ==> 0.44%'
rand1m                    exit 0, 'Compressed 1048576 bytes into 1048595 bytes ==> 100.00%'
fifo (default or explicit out) exit 0, streams fine
symlink                   followed; output named <linkname>.lz4; mode/mtime from the target
/proc/self/cmdline        exit 0 (streamed; st_size==0 is not trusted), 87 -> 106 bytes
no args at all, stdin=/dev/null, stdout=file  -> 15-byte empty frame on stdout, exit 0, stderr empty
```

## 11. Progress / summary format (stderr, printed even when stderr is a plain file)
```
b'\rRead : <MiB> MiB   ==> <pct>%   '          # pct = 100*out/in, 2 decimals
b'\r' + 79 spaces + b'\r'                      # clear line
b'Compressed <inBytes> bytes into <outBytes> bytes ==> <pct>%\n'
```
`<MiB>` is an integer count of MiB read (`0` for small files, `1` for 1 MiB). On a fatal write error the clear-line
and summary are replaced in place: `b'\rRead : 1 MiB   ==> 100.00%   Error 42 : ...'`.

## 12. Misc argument handling
* `--` ends option parsing: `executable -- -c f` treats `-c` as the **input** filename
  -> `b'-c: No such file or directory \n'`, exit 1.
* A file whose name begins with `-` is usable via a path prefix (`/dir/-f` works).
* `-v` adds: banner, `Using 55 threads for compression \n` (machine-dependent), and
  `Done in 0.00 s ==> <rate> MiB/s  (cpu load : NN%)\n` (rate can be absurd for tiny inputs,
  e.g. `274023615030868704.00 MiB/s`).
* `-B4` adds `b'using blocks of size 64 KB \n'` before the progress line.

```
0    success
1    declined overwrite / missing or unreadable input / directory input / unwritable or
     unopenable output / name too long / "won't be used" arg error / console refusals
42   write error detected (output > 4096 bytes)
44   Unrecognized header (accidental decompression of a .lz4-named plain file)
50   --rm unlink failure
141  killed by SIGPIPE (128+13)
153  killed by SIGXFSZ (128+25)
```

## compress-basic — exactly-reproducible facts (lz4 v1.10.0 CLI)

STREAMS: every diagnostic (notice/progress/summary/prompt/error) → stderr. stdout carries payload only when the destination is stdout.

DEFAULT OUTPUT NAME: `.lz4` is always **appended verbatim** — no stripping, no case folding, no "already has suffix" warning.
`small→small.lz4`, `f.txt→f.txt.lz4`, `dot.→dot..lz4`, `.hidden→.hidden.lz4`, `x.LZ4→x.LZ4.lz4` (uppercase not recognised), `"a b.txt"→"a b.txt.lz4"`, newline-in-name fine.
Auto-derived names print `"Compressed filename will be : <out> \n"` (trailing space before `\n`). Never printed when an explicit 2nd positional arg is given, nor with `-q`, nor when output is stdout.

`.lz4`-NAMED INPUT: default mode = decompression. `executable z.lz4` (plain text) → exit **44**, `"Decoding file z \nError 44 : Unrecognized header : file cannot be decoded \n"`, and **leaves a 0-byte file `z`**. Level flags (`-9`) and `-c` do NOT force compression; only `-z` does. `-z`/`-d`: last flag wins. File named exactly `.lz4` → stripped name is the directory: `"Decoding file /dir/ \n/dir/ already exists; ..."`, exit 1.

OUTPUT EXISTS: prompts **identically with and without a tty** (verified via pty). Never auto-declines on non-tty.
`"<out> already exists; do you want to overwrite (y/N) ? "` (no newline, one trailing space), then reads a line from stdin.
- first char `y`/`Y` (incl. `yes`) → proceeds, exit 0
- anything else (`n`,`N`,empty,`junk`,`ny`) or EOF → appends `"    not overwritten  \n"` (4 spaces before, 2 after; 5 spaces total after `?`), **exit 1**
- **stdin an open pipe with no data → blocks forever**
`-q`/`-qq`/`-qqq`: no prompt, `"<out> already exists; not overwritten  \n"`, exit 1.
`-f`: silent overwrite exit 0. `-f -q`: completely silent. Existence test is a stat, so an output that is a **directory** also prompts; with `-f` → `"<out>: Is a directory\n"` exit 1.

`-k` / `--rm`: `-k` is the default and a no-op. `--rm` unlinks the source **silently** on success. Last flag wins (`--rm -k` keeps, `-k --rm` removes). `--rm` removes a symlink source (target survives) and a fifo source; fires even when destination is stdout/`null`/`/dev/null`; does NOT fire if the output could not be opened. Unlink failure → `"Error 50 : Remove error : <src>: Permission denied \n"`, **exit 50**.

PERMISSIONS/MTIME: no temp file — the destination is written **directly under its final name**. Created with `0666 & ~umask`; the source's mode is applied only **after** success (proved with `ulimit -f 1`: umask 077+src 644 → partial 600; umask 000+src 600 → partial 666). On success output gets the source's **exact mode** (setuid preserved: 4755→4755) and **exact mtime** (future mtimes too), for explicit output names as well. As root the output is chowned to the source uid/gid; as non-root the chown fails silently. **Metadata copy is skipped for non-regular sources** (fifo 666→out 644, `/dev/null` 666→out 644).

SPECIAL NAMES (exact string, case-sensitive, no path form): input `-` and `stdin` = stdin; output `-` and `stdout` = stdout; output `null` = discard. `STDOUT`, `NULL`, `./stdin`, `/abs/stdin`, `/abs/stdout`, `/abs/null` are ordinary files. A real file named `stdin` is ignored when addressed as bare `stdin`.
Writing to stdout **lowers display level by 1** → stderr entirely empty for `-c`, `-`, `stdout`, and no-input-file. `-v` restores banner+progress+summary. Output `null` and `/dev/null` still print the normal summary (exit 0, no `null` file created).
`-c` does NOT consume a 2nd positional arg: `-c src out` → `"Error : out won't be used ! Do you want multiple input files (-m) ? \n"` exit 1.

CONSOLE REFUSALS (stderr): `"refusing to read from a console\n"` (no trailing space) exit 1 — no input file, or input `-`, with tty stdin. `"refusing to write to console without -c \n"` (trailing space) exit 1 — destination stdout with tty stdout. `-c` on a tty writes raw frame bytes to the terminal, exit 0, stderr empty.

ERROR STRINGS — input-open failures end `" \n"`, output-open failures end `"\n"`:
```
"lz4: <path> is a directory -- ignored \n"                 exit 1  (no output created)
"<path>: No such file or directory \n"                     exit 1  (also with -f; also dangling symlink)
"<path>: Permission denied \n"                             exit 1  (unreadable input)
"<out>: Permission denied\n"                               exit 1  (unwritable dir or file)
"<out>: No such file or directory\n"                       exit 1  (nonexistent output dir)
"<out>: File name too long\n"                              exit 1  (auto name > NAME_MAX; 253-char input)
"<out>: Is a directory\n"                                  exit 1  (with -f)
"Error : <arg3> won't be used ! Do you want multiple input files (-m) ? \n"  exit 1
"Error 42 : Write error : failed writing single-block compressed frame \n"   exit 42
```
The directory / missing / unreadable cases still print `Compressed filename will be : ...` first.

SILENTLY-LOST WRITE ERRORS: if total output ≤ 4096 bytes the failing destination is not detected. `-f <n bytes> /dev/full` reports **success exit 0** for n = 100/1000/2000/3000/4000 (out = n+19), for `empty` (15 B) and `zeros64k` (286 B); from n = 4090 (out 4109) upward → `Error 42` exit 42. ```

executable -f s s     -> exit 0, "Compressed 0 bytes into 15 bytes ==> 1500.00%";

PROGRESS/SUMMARY (stderr, emitted even when stderr is a plain file):
```
"\rRead : <N> MiB   ==> <pct>%   "      N = integer MiB read; pct = 100*out/in, 2 decimals
"\r" + 79 spaces + "\r"
"Compressed <in> bytes into <out> bytes ==> <pct>%\n"
```
On a fatal write error the clear-line/summary are replaced in place: `"\rRead : 1 MiB   ==> 100.00%   Error 42 : ...\n"`.

MISC: `--` ends option parsing (`-- -c f` → `-c` is the input → `"-c: No such file or directory \n"` exit 1).
